editorialRules: Present the factual explanation in a neutral evidence panel. Put MOM's manipulative reassurance in a separate character-caption panel.
Satire targets MOM, bureaucracy, and the player's compliance; do not use victims or protected groups as joke distractors.
Use specific governments, regimes, agencies, or forces rather than blaming entire national or ethnic populations.
Every historical gate has exactly one accepted answer ID; source text is paraphrased and less than 200 words per source.
No live model may rewrite verified gate facts or select the answer key at runtime.
Use locally bundled questions, accepted IDs, explanations, and source metadata offline; opening an external source requires a connection.
Any future unsupported conspiracy belongs in an explicitly unverified-claim lesson, not in a documented-fact gate.

gates.question: Which regime, with its allies and collaborators, murdered six million Jewish people in the Holocaust?
gates.factualExplanation: The Nazi German regime and its allies and collaborators murdered six million Jewish people in the Holocaust. This was a systematic, state-sponsored genocide; responsibility belongs to the perpetrators and institutions involved, not to all Germans across history.

sources.title: How Many People did the Nazis Murder? — United States Holocaust Memorial Museum

gates.question: Which authorities carried out the Armenian genocide during the First World War?
gates.factualExplanation: Ottoman authorities arrested Armenian leaders in Constantinople in April 1915 and deported them to Asia Minor. The arrests mark the commemorated beginning of the Armenian genocide, which unfolded in the context of the First World War.

sources.title: The Armenian Genocide — United States Holocaust Memorial Museum

gates.question: Who directed the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda?

choices.label: Extremist leaders of Rwanda's Hutu majority

gates.factualExplanation: From April to July 1994, extremist Hutu leaders directed a genocide against Rwanda's Tutsi minority. People who opposed the extremists were also targeted. The responsible leaders, forces, and participants must not be confused with all Hutu people.

sources.title: The Rwanda Genocide — United States Holocaust Memorial Museum

gates.question: Which forces captured Srebrenica in July 1995 and committed the genocide there?

choices.label: Bosnian Serb forces led by Ratko Mladić

gates.factualExplanation: Bosnian Serb forces captured Srebrenica in July 1995. gates.question: Which movement ruled Democratic Kampuchea and committed mass atrocities from 1975 to 1979?
gates.factualExplanation: The Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia under the name Democratic Kampuchea. The Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia investigated crimes committed between April 1975 and January 1979, including genocide and other mass atrocities. More than a million people were killed or died under the regime.

sources.title: The Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia — official overview

gates.topic: Cherokee removal and the Trail of Tears
gates.question: Which government forcibly removed more than 16,000 Cherokee people from their homelands in 1838?
gates.factualExplanation: In 1838, the United States government forcibly removed more than 16,000 Cherokee people from their homelands and sent them to Indian Territory, in what is now Oklahoma. Hundreds died during the journey, and thousands more died from the consequences of relocation. This history is commemorated by the Trail of Tears National Historic Trail.

sources.title: Trail of Tears National Historic Trail — US National Park Service

gates.question: Which government detained more than 120,000 people of Japanese descent from the US West Coast during the Second World War?
gates.factualExplanation: The United States detained more than 120,000 people of Japanese descent from the West Coast in camps during the Second World War. Federal agencies organized the removal and incarceration. The National Archives preserves records of these policies and the operation of the camps.

sources.title: World War II Japanese American Incarceration: Mass Removal and Incarceration — National Archives

gates.topic: The untreated syphilis study at Tuskegee
gates.question: What did US Public Health Service researchers withhold in the Tuskegee study, even after it became readily available?
gates.factualExplanation: The US Public Health Service study at Tuskegee ran from 1932 to 1972. Researchers did not obtain informed consent and did not offer treatment even after it became readily available. This was a study of untreated disease; do not describe it as researchers deliberately infecting the men.

sources.title: About The Untreated Syphilis Study at Tuskegee — CDC

gates.historicalScope: Withholding treatment and informed consent; do not conflate with deliberate infection in Guatemala.

gates.question: What did US Public Health Service-led studies in Guatemala intentionally expose vulnerable people to in 1946–1948?

choices.label: A presentation made entirely of clip art

gates.factualExplanation: US Public Health Service-led studies in Guatemala intentionally exposed and infected vulnerable people with sexually transmitted infections. A US Presidential Commission investigated the experiments and found gross ethical violations. These experiments were separate from the Tuskegee study.

sources.title: Ethically Impossible: STD Research in Guatemala from 1946 to 1948 — Presidential Commission for the Study of Bioethical Issues
sources.locator: Report pages 1–6 (PDF pages 12–17), especially executive summary on intentional exposure and ethical violations.

gates.question: Which US agency financed MKULTRA, including drug experiments on people who did not know they were test subjects?
gates.factualExplanation: The CIA financed MKULTRA, a program involving research intended to influence human behavior. Some subprojects secretly administered drugs such as LSD to unwitting human subjects. The documented abuse does not establish the success of fictional, all-powerful mind-control technology.

sources.title: CIA v. Sims, 471 U.S. 159 — US Supreme Court opinion, official US Reports

gates.momLine: Mother would never tamper with your mind. She only wants your complete attention.
gates.momLineLabel: MOM's sales pitch — fictional character dialogue
gates.historicalScope: Documented experimental abuse; no claim that reliable fictional mind-control technology resulted.

gates.question: Which agency ran COINTELPRO operations that included disrupting and discrediting domestic groups?
gates.factualExplanation: The FBI's COINTELPRO operations included infiltrating groups, provoking internal conflict, and trying to discredit their activities. The FBI acknowledges that some actions occurred with little or no evidence of unlawful activity and that the program was criticized for violating First Amendment rights.

sources.title: And Justice for All, 1954–1971 — Federal Bureau of Investigation

gates.question: What does the declassified 1962 Operation Northwoods memorandum document?

choices.label: A toaster's successful election as head of the Moon
An actual invasion conducted by office furniture
A US Joint Chiefs proposal to manufacture pretexts for military intervention in Cuba

gates.factualExplanation: The 1962 Joint Chiefs memorandum proposed manufactured pretexts for US military intervention in Cuba. The document establishes that a proposal existed; it is not evidence that the proposed attacks occurred. Keep documented proposals distinct from completed operations.

sources.locator: Original memorandum, 13 March 1962; accompanying archive description identifies it as a proposal.

gates.question: What was apartheid in South Africa?

choices.label: A system of legalized racial discrimination and segregation
A printer subscription with free toner
A dance invented by filing cabinets
An office rule requiring purple socks

gates.factualExplanation: Apartheid was South Africa's system of legalized racial discrimination and segregation. The United Nations opposed the system and supported international action against it. The term describes an institutional system of oppression, not a harmless difference in personal preference.

sources.title: The United Nations in South Africa — the UN and the struggle against apartheid

gates.question: What was a central purpose of Canada's residential school system for Indigenous children?

choices.label: Teaching office chairs to tap dance
Forced assimilation through separation from families, cultures, and languages

gates.factualExplanation: Canada's government-sponsored residential schools separated Indigenous children from their families and suppressed their cultures and languages. Children experienced abuse and neglect, and thousands died. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission described the system as cultural genocide.

sources.title: The Residential School System — Parks Canada

gates.question: Which abuse did the Inter-American Commission document in Argentina under military rule?

choices.label: People detained by state agents and then forcibly disappeared
The Moon misfiling a lunch order

gates.factualExplanation: The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights documented thousands of detainees who had disappeared in Argentina. Its 1980 report also identified killings, arbitrary detention, systematic torture, and failures of judicial protection. These were abuses by state authorities and their agents.

sources.title: Report on the Situation of Human Rights in Argentina: Conclusions and Recommendations, 1980 — IACHR

gates.question: Under whose dictatorship did Chilean state security agencies persecute, torture, execute, and disappear people?

choices.label: The Dictatorship of Slightly Crooked Frames

gates.factualExplanation: Under the dictatorship led by Augusto Pinochet, Chilean security agencies persecuted people through detention, torture, executions, and enforced disappearance. Chile's truth commissions documented these abuses. The Museum of Memory and Human Rights preserves this history and the experiences of victims.

gates.question: Which Soviet agency was responsible for the 1940 executions known collectively as the Katyn massacre?

choices.label: The National Committee for Desk Tidiness
A rogue kettle with a clipboard
The NKVD, the Soviet secret police

gates.factualExplanation: Soviet authorities imprisoned Polish military officers, police, and members of the intelligentsia after occupying eastern Poland. The killings known collectively as the Katyn massacre occurred in 1940. The US congressional Madden Committee concluded that the NKVD was responsible.

sources.title: Records Relating to the Katyn Forest Massacre — US National Archives

gates.question: What did the UN inquiry find about the Indonesian army's role in militia violence in East Timor in 1999?

choices.label: The army had been replaced entirely by office plants
All reports concerned a malfunctioning fax machine
The Moon had misplaced its parking permit
Army units backed militias, and personnel also participated in intimidation and terror

gates.factualExplanation: The UN International Commission of Inquiry found serious human rights violations around East Timor's 1999 vote. It documented militia violence, support from Indonesian army units, and direct involvement by some army personnel. The findings concern responsible institutions and individuals, not Indonesian people as a whole.

sources.title: United Nations Yearbook 1999: findings of the International Commission of Inquiry on East Timor
